canonical_name: Eulerian-trail existence characterization family (exact variant open)
literal_source_claim_zh: 欧拉路径存在的充要条件
literal_source_claim_en: Necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of an Eulerian path.
statement_blocker: The catalog says only that necessary and sufficient conditions exist. It does not state them, choose simple versus multi- or directed graphs, fix finiteness, decide full-graph versus non-isolated connectivity, choose fixed or existential endpoints, say whether circuits count as paths, or settle empty and edgeless cases. Selecting one exact proposition at intake would invent missing mathematics.
candidate_claim_not_credited_as_statemen: A finite undirected graph has a trail using every edge exactly once iff all non-isolated vertices lie in one connected component and exactly zero or two vertices have odd degree, with endpoint refinements in the two-odd case; the exact source variant and encoding remain open.

canonical_formal_target.candidate_relationship: definition and necessary direction only; the module explicitly marks the converse existence theorem as TODO

domain_and_universes: Candidate scope ranges over a finite undirected graph on a universe-polymorphic vertex type, potentially a multigraph to preserve the historical bridge model. The graph representation, finiteness instances, decidable equality/adjacency, universe, endpoints, and connectivity predicate remain statement-phase decisions.
conclusion: Open as an exact expression: existence of an Eulerian trail, with fixed or existential endpoints, characterized by a source-selected connectivity and degree-parity condition.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded at intake; the statement must settle empty, singleton, edgeless, isolated-vertex, one-edge, path, cycle, disconnected edge-support, zero-odd, two-odd, and equal-endpoint cases.
